consumerAdoption: Host/desktop durable-operation and error-contract matrix verified by main/services/aiden-remote-durable-operation.test.ts and cross-checked against bot-outbox-delivery.json. Native clients adopt it in their own suites, and neither matches it yet. Both still ship route-specific before-effect allowlists of the 13 core codes, and the iOS and Android Resume classifiers treat 409 revision_conflict as ambiguous. The planned iOS adoption is one shared allowlist for every strict before-effect route that equals recognizedBeforeEffectCodes; Android needs the same change. This fixture's test does not check either client. Both clients keep an attempt uncertain once an earlier try of it was ambiguous, whatever a later response to that attempt says.
description: Host/desktop durable-operation and error-classification failure-ambiguity matrix for Aiden Remote idempotent mutations, verified by main/services/aiden-remote-durable-operation.test.ts. Compares beforeEffectRefusal (fail-closed pre-effect refusal codes proven before any side effect, including 409 revision_conflict, which assertRevision raises before any write, but excluding replayed 409 internal_error) against cachedRejectionLedger (executeAidenDurableOperation routes backed by AidenIdempotencyLedger where settled rejections are cached for 24h and unrecorded/unknown outcomes return 409 idempotency_in_flight).

policies.beforeEffectRefusal: Only a structured non-transient 4xx response (400-499 excluding 408 and 429) whose error code is on recognizedBeforeEffectCodes proves no side effect occurred on a non-ledger before-effect route. 409 revision_conflict is a recognized refusal: assertRevision rejects a stale revision before the action writes anything, and the ledger replays that same refusal under the key. 409 idempotency_in_flight (including post-effect authorization loss on Bot peers and open-work), 409 internal_error, unknown codes, 408/429/5xx, unparsed HTTP responses, transport losses, and cancellations remain ambiguous.
policies.cachedRejectionLedger: Backed by executeAidenDurableOperation and AidenIdempotencyLedger. Structured non-transient 4xx responses (including replayed settled rejections such as 409 revision_conflict, 409 internal_error, and 409 idempotency_conflict) settle the attempt; 409 idempotency_in_flight, 408/429/5xx, unparsed HTTP responses, transport losses, and cancellations remain ambiguous so the caller retains its idempotency key.
